key_insight: DrugGen-2 generates small molecules using both disease ontology and target protein sequence, improving disease-aware drug design over target-only approaches.
engineering_relevance: The model shows how conditioning generation on biomedical context and optimizing with reinforcement learning can improve candidate quality for AI-assisted drug discovery pipelines.
method: Fine-tune GPT-2 on curated drug–disease–target records
Apply supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO reinforcement learning
Reward validity, novelty, diversity, and predicted binding affinity
evidence_signal: On five diabetic nephropathy-related targets, DrugGen-2 outperformed DrugGPT and DrugGen, producing more unique molecules and better predicted affinities; docking found candidates as strong as -9.917 versus enalapril at -8.283.
watch_item: Results rely on predicted affinity and docking rather than experimental wet-lab validation, so real-world efficacy and safety remain unconfirmed.
paper_title: DrugGen 2: A disease-aware language model for enhancing drug discovery
